newsitem.title: INDIA: India car bomb kills three from official's family.
newsitem.headline: India car bomb kills three from official's family.

text.p: A car bomb killed three members of a local government minister's family on Wednesday in the northeast Indian state of Nagaland, police said.
The wife, daughter and grandchild of K. Hollohan, industry minister of Nagaland, were killed by the bomb which could have been detonated by remote control, police in the state capital Kohima said.
The minister, travelling separately, had passed the spot where the bomb exploded just minutes earlier.
Eleven people were injured by the blast at Arai Mile, near Kohima.
Separatist Maoists from the ethnic Naga tribe are fighting Indian authorities in the state which borders Burma.
Authorities say the Naga rebels are also locked in a bitter feud with rival Kuki tribals for control of National Highway 39, where the blast took place.
The Naga rebels see the Kukis as pro-India. Indian officials say the two tribes are fighting over control of the highway to help smuggle drugs from Burma to Europe and other Western destinations.
